A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with readable text and visuals. All sections, Figures 1–3, Tables 1–12, and Appendices A–C can be matched. The shorter v2 reflects bibliography compression and reflow, not missing research material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Isabelle/HOL evaluations of three LLMs on miniF2F, Def_Wiki, and Def_ArXiv, including numerical performance, refinement experiments, and error analyses in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations, including the numerical results in Tables 3–4 and 8–12, Figures 2–3, and appendix case studies.

M1.justification: Categorical refinement, symbolic refinement, and postprocessing/prompt-based formal definition grounding retain the same procedures. The prompt instructions in Table 7 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same miniF2F mathematical statements and Def_Wiki/Def_ArXiv machine-learning definitions. No dataset, domain, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same DeepSeekMath-7B, Llama3-8B, and GPT-4o models and refinement/grounding variants participate in corresponding comparisons. The added related-work citation does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Both retain the 10/46 Def_Wiki development/test split, 244 miniF2F test samples, 30 Def_ArXiv definitions, greedy decoding, and Isabelle-based Pass, FEO, and error-category metrics. No experimental protocol is revised.

E4.justification: The refinement and grounding analyses in Figures 2–3 are unchanged. Appendices A–B retain the Bradley–Terry grounding case study and the same three incorrect-code examples, with their original explanations.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains the same dataset means and standard deviations. Neither version reports repeated-run or seed-based uncertainty for performance results, and no statistical reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results, and qualitative findings match across versions, including the appendices. For example, GPT-4o zero-shot Pass remains 25.41%, 10.87%, and 13.33% on miniF2F-Test, Def_Wiki-Test, and Def_ArXiv respectively (Table 3).

T1.justification: The autoformalization mapping in Section 2 and mathematical definitions in the examples are unchanged. No formal assumption, theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s four contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about challenging definition benchmarks, LLM error patterns, and the benefits and limits of refinement and grounding.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning self-correction, contextual definitions, and entangled errors remain unchanged. Section 6 and Appendix A retain the same limitations concerning dataset size, generalization beyond Isabelle/HOL, and semantic consistency.

D1.justification: Dataset collection instructions, decoding information, manual selection of grounding context, prompt templates in Tables 6–7, and the stated code/data access link are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4 moves Li et al. (2024) from the Lean examples to Isabelle and adds Lu et al. (2024), Process-driven autoformalization in Lean 4, as the Lean citation. This is a limited change in literature attribution; the broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Citation wording changes, and lengthy individual-author lists for the Llama 3 and OpenAI reports become team/organization names. These bibliographic edits leave the section order and scientific narrative essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: The condensed bibliography reflows references and the opening appendix case studies, moving Appendix A from page 13 to page 10. Figures and tables retain their designs and contents; later appendix displays shift only in pagination.

improvement.justification: v2 improves literature attribution by adding a specifically identified Lean work and revising the Isabelle/Lean citation grouping in Section 4. Replacing sprawling model-report author lists with organizational names also makes the bibliography easier to scan. These are limited improvements in attribution and readability; the scientific evidence and acknowledged limitations remain unchanged.
